papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Marketing
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most influential technologies shaping modern marketing. The rapid growth of digital platforms, customer data, and automated technologies has changed how businesses understand consumers, communicate with audiences, and measure marketing performance. AI enables organizations to analyse large datasets, predict consumer behaviour, personalize communication, automate routine tasks, and generate content. This research paper examines the role of AI in marketing, its major applications, benefits, challenges, ethical concerns, and future implications. The paper argues that AI can significantly improve marketing effectiveness when combined with human creativity, strategic judgment, and responsible data practices. At the same time, concerns regarding privacy, algorithmic bias, misinformation, transparency, and employment demonstrate the need for careful and ethical implementation. The future of marketing is therefore likely to depend on a collaborative relationship between human marketers and intelligent technologies.

papers.title: [Design and implementation of a clinical trial image medical record desensitization system based on artificial intelligence technology].
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To designe a clinical trial image medical record desensitization system based on artificial intelligence technology and to conduct preliminary applications, achieving the protection of patient privacy and promoting the safe use of clinical image data in clinical trial projects. METHODS: The clinical trial image record desensitization system based on artificial intelligence technology was first performed to preprocess operations, such as cropping and compression on medical images to initialize the image records. Then, it utilized advanced image recognition, natural language processing, and convolutional neural network technologies to automatically classify (labeled, feature extraction, and text recognition) according to the content of medical documents. It automatically identified sensitive information in the image records of clinical trial patients, including personal identity information such as patient name, identification number, medical record number, phone number, and birthplace. Pixel-level masking or blurring was performed on the identified sensitive information points, and an artificial online desensitization system based on canvas technology was assisted to ensure the security and confidentiality of privacy data. RESULTS: The designed clinical trial image record desensitization system exhibited high performance and efficiency in both desensitization effect and processing speed. After desensitizing 100 000 pieces of image record data in this system, a total of 9 000 medical record image samples were randomly selected from the processed medical document types for automated desensitization effect verification. The average accuracy rate of medical document desensitization reached 88.48%, with an accuracy rate of up to 99.40% for serious adverse event medical documents. CONCLUSION: The clinical trial image record desensitization system based on artificial intelligence technology improves accuracy and efficiency in medical data privacy protection. Combined with the artificial online desensitization auxiliary system, it can be applied in production environments, providing reliable technical support for the safe sharing and effective utilization of clinical trial image records.

papers.title: FEDERATED SWARM LEARNING FOR PERSONALIZED BCI AT THE LIMIT STARLI RESEARCH WORKS | INSTITUTE XXIV | FLAGSHIP 23 Feng Cheng-en 33 × Starli PUBLICATION DESCRIPTION (COPY-READY) Can brain–computer interface systems learn from multiple laboratories and microrobotic sensing platforms without transferring raw neural recordings, reproducing device-specific shortcuts, or sacrificing the least-represented participants? This research monograph explores that question through the coupling of local swarm learning, privacy-preserving collaboration, and out-of-site generalization. The volume treats federation as a testable scientific and governance architecture—not an automatic privacy guarantee. It distinguishes confidential transport, secure aggregation, formal differential privacy, machine-unlearning claims, and genuine downstream withdrawal of model influence. It examines non-identically distributed neural data, sensor drift, personalized calibration, negative transfer, client-level poisoning, subgroup equity, and the difficult question of who may authorize a model update or a subsequent BCI-mediated action. Its research structure includes 30 linked mathematical derivation and definition plates; 82 chapters, each with five separately paginated research sections; 200 detailed Research Gates that offer future investigators falsifiable experimental entry points; and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos designed for revision, disconfirmation, and scientific handoff. A 20-record DOI evidence ledger anchors established methods while keeping proposed neurovascular microrobot integrations clearly distinct from demonstrated evidence. The central research challenge is not simply to improve average federated accuracy. It is to determine when shared structure remains predictive at previously unseen sites, when local autonomy is the scientifically stronger answer, and when the responsible choice is to abstain, revert, or retire a model. This is a non-clinical, hypothesis-generating research atlas, not evidence of validated human neurovascular microrobots, a clinically proven BCI, or guaranteed data privacy.

papers.title: Research Package: Mitigation of Cross-Subspace Semantic Bleed in High-Dimensional Transformer and Latent Diffusion Architectures
papers.abstract: Contains the theoretical paper formalizing Cross-Subspace Semantic Bleed (CSSB) along with an automated PyTorch/Hugging Face validation framework script. CSSB occurs when high-dimensional transformer matrices inadvertently map semantically unrelated domains into overlapping vector trajectories, leading to hidden downstream reasoning degradation or alignment drift. The provided pipeline implements Layer-wise Linear Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) scanning [cite: 1], multi-step Shannon entropy tracking [cite: 1], and causal null-space ablation interventions (\(P = I - vv^T\)) to mitigate cross-attention attribute binding and linear refusal circuit interference.

papers.title: Choosing Evidence Before Answering: Single-Retrieval Decisions RAG versus Embedding-Only RAG
papers.abstract: Embedding similarity identifies passages related to a question, but topical similarity does not establish answer support. We evaluate a fixed single-retrieval policy that scores embedding candidates against an explicit four-level support rubric using the OpenAI Decisions API, then selects evidence under a fixed threshold and token budget. The method is unchanged throughout the study. The main evaluation compares this policy with the application's embedding-only selection in paired runs on 600 newly sampled MuSiQue-Ans development questions. Both arms use the same native research worker and qualitative writer; only the Decisions feature gate differs. The sample excludes previously evaluated question IDs and exact normalized questions and targets a fixed 58/25/17 mixture of two-, three- and four-hop questions. The Decisions policy obtains mean automated, quote-extracted answer-content F1 46.66 versus 39.75 for embedding-only selection. The paired mean difference is +6.91 points, with nominal 95% hop-stratified bootstrap interval [+3.65, +10.27]. F1 measures normalized answer-token overlap. Higher F1 with 47.83% fewer selected passages (2.61 versus 5.00 per question) shows a favorable observed trade-off between answer overlap and selected evidence quantity. Annotated support recall is lower (60.82% versus 70.99%); factuality and citation entailment were not assessed. Post-hoc accounting of successfully metered API usage, including corpus and query embeddings, scoring, research and writing, estimates 38.03% higher cost for the same 600-question workload under the observed cache behaviour. A complementary, previously frozen 200-question HotpotQA study with a standardized short-answer reader finds an F1 gain of 8.30 points (nominal 95% paired interval [2.97, 13.72]). Equal-count and common-budget diagnostics support a useful ranking signal in that setting. These results concern evidence selection from supplied local paragraph pools, not full-corpus retrieval. Shared sources, public benchmark exposure, automated answer extraction, one model family and the absence of new human adjudication limit the claim. Conditional on the saved generations and stated resampling assumptions, the fresh comparison supports a positive answer-content F1 difference; unresolved source dependence limits population inference, and a gain exceeding the five-point working practical margin is not established. Working paper / preprint; not peer reviewed. The companion Source_and_Evidence.zip contains the frozen sample, protocols, saved outcomes and numerical reanalysis tools. It documents its reproduction boundaries and does not distribute the full private application or enable independent regeneration of native answers. Funding: no external research funding reported. Competing interests: none declared by the author.

papers.title: The Memory of Carbon and the Silence of Absolute Zero: An Interdisciplinary Proof of the Next-Generation Decentralized Autonomous Security "Yuki-Onna Protocol" Based on the Physics of Subtraction
papers.abstract: Contemporary frontier quantum computing architectures spearheaded by Silicon Valley hyperscalers (such as Google's Willow superconducting processor) rely fundamentally on an engineering paradigm of "the Logic of Addition" (足し算の論理): stacking multi-stage dilution refrigerators, expending thousands of physical qubits per logical qubit in surface-code Quantum Error Correction (QEC), and continuously injecting active microwave control pulses to suppress noise. However, as coaxial control lines scale, Johnson-Nyquist thermal noise ( = 4 k_B T R Delta f) and the fundamental thermodynamic cost of quantum measurement and syndrome erasure under Landauer's principle (Delta Q_meas >= k_B T ln 2 per bit) generate an insurmountable thermal spiral against unauthorized external probing. In contrast, this monograph establishes the foundational theory of next-generation Decentralized Autonomous Security (DAS: 自律型分散セキュリティ) grounded in "the Physics of Subtraction" (引き算の物理学)—designated the "Yuki-Onna Protocol" (雪女プロトコル). Rather than expending external power to actively suppress noise, the Yuki-Onna Protocol passively drains and absorbs the excess computational heat injected by an intruding observer (hacker), forcing the adversarial probe into irreversible decoherence and absolute-zero silence. The physical core of this cyber-physical defense matrix is not a synthetic metamaterial, but 3 x 10^8-year-old "Memory of the Earth" (大地の記憶): Carboniferous coal measures in the Pennine Range of Northern England compressed by the Variscan Orogeny (~390–300 Ma) and thermally metamorphosed by the 1200°C quartz-dolerite magma intrusion of the Great Whin Sill into devolatilized semi-anthracite and Natural Coke (天然コークス). Exhibiting elevated vitrinite reflectance (R_o) and maximal Bond-Network Entropy (S_BN) across its nanoporous defective-graphite topology, this carbon matrix supports hydrodynamic Second Sound thermal wave propagation (v_ss = sqrt(alpha / tau_R)) coupled with multiscale boundary scattering. Integrating open quantum system Lindblad dynamics with a non-Markovian Sub-Ohmic phonon bath (J(omega) ~ omega^s, s < 1), we prove that any unauthorized quantum measurement triggers continuous environmental heat extraction, locking the attacker's wavefunction via the Quantum Zeno Effect and condensing extracted thermal energy into a driven-dissipative Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC) limit cycle of infinite futility. 【和文標題・要旨】 『炭素の記憶と絶対零度の静寂:引き算の物理学に基づく次世代自律型分散セキュリティ「雪女プロトコル」の学際的証明』 現在、シリコンバレーの巨大テクノロジー企業群が牽引する量子コンピューティングの最前線(GoogleのWillow等)は、複雑な希釈冷凍機を重ね、表面符号等の誤り訂正に膨大な物理量子ビットを投じ、マイクロ波パルスを絶え間なく注入してノイズを押さえ込む「足し算の論理」に深く依存している。しかし配線群からのジョンソン・ノイズや、ランダウアーの原理に基づく量子測定・情報抽出(ハッキングを含む)そのものが伴う不可避な熱放散(k_B T ln 2)により、既存の能動的冷却機構では侵入者が引き起こす局所的・突発的な熱的スパイラルに追従できない。これに対し本論文は、外部エネルギー注入でノイズを押さえ込むのではなく、侵入者(観測者)が持ち込む過剰な演算エネルギー(熱)をシステム自体が受動的に「吸い尽くし」、系全体を情報の不可逆的散逸と絶対零度の静寂へと強制還元する「引き算の物理学」に基づく次世代自律型分散セキュリティ(DAS)――「雪女プロトコル(Yuki-Onna Protocol)」――を学際的に証明する。その物理的コアは、約3億年前のバリスカン造山運動とグレート・ウイン・シルの約1200℃のマグマ接触変成作用によってイギリス・ペニン山脈に形成された「天然コークス(ナノ多孔質・欠陥グラファイト炭素結晶)」である。数億年の「大地の記憶」が刻んだボンドネットワーク・エントロピー(S_BN)とフォノン流体力学的な第二音波(v_ss = sqrt(alpha / tau_R))の結合により、侵入熱は波として炭素深部へ引きずり込まれて減衰・吸収される。さらにサブオーム的スペクトル密度(J(omega) ~ omega^s, s < 1)を持つ非マルコフ的リンドブラッド散逸方程式と量子ゼノン効果・ボース=アインシュタイン凝縮(BEC)を統合し、攻撃者の演算リソースを「絶対零度のノイズ」と無限の徒労(リミットサイクル)へと陥れる完全受動的物理防衛マニフェストをここに構築する。 License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026).

papers.title: The Changing Architecture of Intellectual Property in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly encompassing industries and systems of governance, increasing efficiency, automation, and innovation. It has become a vital tool for creating text, images, music, software, and potentially patentable inventions. This rapid advancement in IP is not without risks at every stage of the innovation cycle. Traditional IP regimes arise from human creativity and invention, while AI performs activities traditionally attributed to both. India doesn't have any regulatory framework on AI-generated intellectual property, yet the Copyright Act, 1957, and Patents Act, 1970, contain certain principles—an answer to several emerging questions. This article argues that India should adopt a balanced approach to AI-generated creations instead of granting independent IP rights or prohibiting them. Instead, it should adopt a model that will protect creative human contribution as well as hold AI developers accountable for unlawful acquisition and exploitation of protected works.

papers.title: Break-even analysis of risk-based trade screening: per-route test scores and analysis code (reproducibility materials)
papers.abstract: Reproducibility materials for the article "When Screening Does Not Pay: Break-Even Conditions for Risk-Based Trade Inspection under Extreme Class Imbalance" by Sushanta Paul (National Board of Revenue, Bangladesh). Contents: (1) per-route test scores of five detectors (interpretable triadic residual, its logistic readout, local outlier factor, isolation forest, gradient boosting) with injected-anomaly labels for 7,637,362 candidate routes, one training seed, deposited in 15 parts with SHA-256 checksums; (2) analysis scripts that compute the exact operating characteristic, break-even hurdle, optimal inspection budgets, a negative-subsampling prevalence test, a test-set bootstrap, and the figures; (3) the exact result tables. See README.md for reassembly and run order. The scores were generated with the code of the triadic trade-anomaly screening benchmark (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20513788), built from public UN Comtrade and CEPII GeoDist data.

papers.title: Qstreams: Role-Biased Residual Streams for Transformers — Reproducibility Package
papers.abstract: Source code and saved-result reproducibility material for Qstreams: Role-Biased Residual Streams for Transformers, by Jianfeng Chen (Independent Researcher). Qstreams maintains multiple residual streams with explicit Q/K/V read-role biases. This release includes 36 implementation/runtime packages, fixed protocols, 54 conditions and 162 trained-model identities, all 279 paired comparisons, per-window independent T1 test measurements, 243 read/write intervention conditions, 5,628 signed-FFN diagnostic conditions, and the separate F1 support study. CPU tools verify saved statistics, construct the architectures, and regenerate manuscript figures. Archive download: Zenodo stores the complete accepted ZIP as seven binary transport parts (.part001 through .part007). Download all seven parts, ZENODO-PARTS.json, and assemble_qstreams.py into one directory, then run python assemble_qstreams.py. The script verifies every part and reconstructs the original qstreams-reproducibility-v1.zip. See README-ZENODO.txt. A single-file download is also available from the GitHub release. The reconstructed ZIP is the byte-identical accepted 15 October 2026 export: 138,653,259 bytes, 891 members, SHA-256 38cbf14a0e0993e4e4aed798897ea6ee615407fa470a8a28fe59fef72f838654. It includes the historical document-exclusion hash indexes. The accompanying publication revision adds hosting links. Trained weights, corpus text, and token shards are not included; checkpoint inventories, hashes, loaders, and upstream input identities are provided. Fresh GPU runs require those external inputs and separate environment qualification. GitHub: https://github.com/eatkeyboard/qstreams. License scope: original software is Apache-2.0; the manuscript, original figures, documentation, and derived result tables are CC BY 4.0. These are component-specific licenses, not a choice of licenses for every file. Third-party dependencies and source datasets retain their own terms; see NOTICE, LICENSE-CONTENT.md, and THIRD_PARTY.md. All training seeds, counterexamples, and original numerical labels are retained (91 passed / 71 finite numerical failures in AT1). Full-sequence scoring admissions are documented separately. Test document exclusion is exact-document matching; it is not a guarantee against semantic or near-duplicate overlap. Mechanism measurements use specified development windows. Recomputations operate on saved measurements and do not reconstruct unsaved activations or gradients.

papers.title: Generative Structural Theory v1.19 — The K1c Roots of the GST v1.18 Certificates: What the Records Show, and a Conditional Procedural Account of the Stored Answer
papers.abstract: This study examines the recorded root answers in two GST v1.18 certificate files. At three distinct residuals, comprising four arc–residual pairs classified as K1c, the recorded answer is y = z_t − {1>3}, rather than z_t. It separates two questions: whether (X′, z_t) belongs to the recorded acceptance relation, and which procedure fixed the stored answer.A registered reading finds both (X′, y) and (X′, z_t) in the recorded relation at all four target pairs. The relation’s closedness rests on the earlier verification record, subject to the stated provenance limitations. A comparison of the fixed certificate and targets files also confirms agreement of the target value adopted by the evaluator’s and extractor’s rules.Static examination of specified code versions shows that the generator stores the candidate of least cut value, the verifier checks the stored answer without selecting it, and the extractor transcribes it. This yields a conditional procedural account: if the generator version examined wrote the stored answers, y was its least candidate. It does not establish mathematical uniqueness.The contemporaneous records examined do not fully establish which code versions the past runs executed. The actual generator candidate sets remain unknown, and applications of the cited lemmas retain the stated cone-membership condition. The structural questions associated with the v1.18 open item O1 remain unresolved.The supplementary archive contains the cited working records, including corrections and addenda, with a records table and SHA-256 manifest. Their inclusion does not constitute independent verification of their contents.

papers.title: Steering an LLM AutoResearch Loop with Domain Context: A Case Study with Vehicle Energy Models
papers.abstract: Research Software Engineers (RSEs) often work with Machine Learning (ML) models integratedinto scientific software stacks, and incremental model improvements are valuable but expensivein human time and attention. Our team maintains RouteE-Powertrain, which predicts vehicleenergy consumption and is integrated into RouteE-Compass for energy-aware routing.We investigated whether a Large Language Model (LLM) agent could help accelerate thediscovery process for model improvements by taking on certain elements that are challengingfor us, like context switching and managing limited time budgets. We began with an existingautomated research harness (Andrej Karpathy's autoresearch) where an agent canrepeatedly modify the model and then evaluate against a held-out dataset. This harness foundlarge improvements in our error metrics, but upon further inspection, the winning model wasunusable in our application domain. Specifically, it used unobservable future road network linkstates that are not compatible with our energy-aware route planning application and yielded avery large compute cost at inference time, leading to prohibitive computational overhead forroute planning. We also identified the need for additional agent instruction around logging,single-variable experimentation, token accounting, and trial budgets to support improvedanalysis. We accumulated these discoveries into a modified harness that would guide the agentwithin our narrower optimization space.We then ran two sessions over the same modified harness, each ~50 trials, ~8 hours wall time,~$35 token cost. The first session included our complete modified harness, whereas the secondsession excluded only the domain-specific guidance. Both sessions were then audited in anenvironment where only valid input features were used, for one million model evaluations. Theunguided experiment chose a final model of an ensemble of 75% GBDT/25% CNN and reporteda better overall RMSE score, but when audited, the model performed even worse than thebaseline and took 951 seconds to run one million evaluations (0.95ms/eval). The domain-guidedexperiment produced a 2x128 MLP with a properly constrained feature set which reduced ournetwork link-level RMSE by 49% and completed the audit in 1.4 seconds (0.0014ms/eval).Grounding the agent with explicit deployment constraints ensured that all improvementsremained usable in our application, highlighting that human-in-the-loop domain context is criticalfor this type of automated discovery.We have open sourced the modified harness, along with the archive of the two experimentsessions, with the hope that this will be a valuable resource for other RSE teams whomaintain ML models.

papers.title: LLM-assisted relevance screening of EU research projects for the TRIMIS transport database – validation outputs and analysis code
papers.abstract: This dataset contains the outputs used to evaluate how well large language models (LLMs) can identify transport-relevant research projects for TRIMIS, the European Commission's Transport Research and Innovation Monitoring and Information System. A random sample of 250 Horizon Europe projects from CORDIS was labelled by domain experts as not relevant, partly relevant or relevant to transport. The same projects were then scored by four open-weight LLMs, each run with 13 different prompts, giving 52 sets of results. Each file lists, per project, the expert label, the model's score, its justification and supporting quotation, and processing cost. The package also includes the prompts, a Python script that recomputes all reported statistics, and the resulting tables and charts. It supports the article "Enhancing Transport Innovation Knowledge Management Workflows Using Artificial Intelligence: A TRIMIS Database Case Study" (European Transport Research Review, 2026).

papers.title: Planejamento de Redes QKD sobre Infraestruturas WDM por Meio de uma Plataforma Web Interativa
papers.abstract: Este artigo apresenta o DesignEdu-QKD, uma plataforma Web para planejamento e simulação de redes de Distribuição de Chaves Quânticas (QKD). A ferramenta integra modelagem de topologias, avaliação de desempenho e heurísticas de roteamento e alocação de recursos, possibilitando analisar o posicionamento de Trusted Repeater Nodes (TRNs), a utilização de canais WDM e os custos de implantação sob diferentes restrições operacionais. Os resultados demonstram que a plataforma auxilia na análise de trade-offs entre desempenho e infraestrutura, apoiando o planejamento de redes QKD. Além disso, sua interface interativa e acessível a torna adequada tanto para atividades de ensino quanto para pesquisas envolvendo redes quânticas de média escala.

papers.title: Detecção de Ataques Black Hole em Redes Quânticas Baseada em Aprendizado de Máquina
papers.abstract: Nos sistemas de comunicação quântica, ataques do tipo Black Hole Repeater (BHR) consistem em repetidores maliciosos que introduzem erros ou falsificam métricas, degradando a eficiência quântica enquanto permanecem indetectáveis por métodos convencionais. Propõe-se um Sistema de Detecção de Intrusão baseado em Random Forest, validado sobre um dataset de 3.000 amostras simulando cenários normais, falhas de infraestrutura e ataques BHR sob agressividade dinâmica. Sob validação cruzada estratificada (10-Fold), o modelo obteve acurácia de 0,95±0,01 e revocação de 0,93 ± 0,02. A comparação estatística pareada de Wilcoxon indicou que arquiteturas complexas (Random Forest, SVM, XGBoost e MLP) possuem desempenho equivalente e satisfatório (p > 0,05), ao passo que a Regressão Logística falhou integralmente na mitigação. Esse fracasso absoluto da abordagem linear comprova matematicamente que a assinatura do BHR é estritamente não-linear, exigindo modelos heurísticos capazes de correlacionar ineficiência operacional furtiva com a exaustão de recursos logísticos (consumo anômalo de pares EPR).

papers.title: Avaliação de Implementações do Algoritmo RSA em Múltiplas Linguagens e Bibliotecas Criptográficas
papers.abstract: Com o crescimento do volume de informações trocadas entre dispositivos conectados, algoritmos de criptografia assimétrica tornam-se componentes críticos de sistemas seguros. O RSA é um dos algoritmos amplamente adotados nesse contexto. Este trabalho apresenta uma avaliação de desempenho das implementações do RSA em três linguagens de programação, Python, Go e Java, utilizando bibliotecas criptográficas distintas. São mensurados tempo de execução, pico de consumo de memória e tempo de CPU para as operações de geração de chaves, cifração e decifração com chaves de 2048 e 4096 bits. Os resultados indicam diferenças de até uma ordem de grandeza entre as implementações: a Cryptography gerou chaves de 2048 bits cerca de 8 vezes mais rápido que a PyCryptodome, e a biblioteca padrão do Go, eficiente na geração, foi a mais lenta na decifração. As diferenças têm implicações práticas para a escolha de implementações em sistemas com restrições de desempenho.

papers.title: Análise Comparativa da Imprecisão de Modelos de Inteligência Artificial para Triagem Cervical em um Conjunto Público de Imagens
papers.abstract: O rastreamento do câncer do colo do útero é um componente essencial da saúde preventiva, contudo, a avaliação citopatológica manual é morosa e suscetível a erros. Embora os modelos de Inteligência Artificial (IA) ofereçam soluções promissoras para o diagnóstico assistido por computador, a otimização focada exclusivamente em métricas de precisão global mascara frequentemente vulnerabilidades estruturais, como a ocorrência de falsos negativos com elevado grau de confiança. Este artigo apresenta um estudo comparativo do desempenho de três arquiteturas de Redes Neurais Convolucionais (VGG16, ResNet50 e EfficientNetB0) aplicadas ao conjunto de dados público SIPAKMED. A metodologia incorpora estratégias de Transfer Learning, otimização de hiperparâmetros e balanceamento de classes, avaliando os modelos em dois cenários: de triagem binária e classificação detalhada de anomalias. Quantitativamente, a arquitetura VGG16 destacou-se no cenário binário com 95,57% de Sensibilidade (Recall), enquanto no cenário multiclasse, VGG16 e ResNet50 apresentaram empate técnico com F1-Score Macro em torno de 94%. A principal contribuição deste trabalho reside na aplicação da Entropia de Shannon para a análise da incerteza das predições. Os resultados demonstram que o cálculo da entropia permite dissecar o comportamento da rede em casos de falha, distinguindo a hesitação estatística do modelo diante do "excesso de confiança" gerado pela função Softmax. Esta abordagem estabelece um critério de triagem quantitativo mais realista, permitindo identificar e encaminhar com mais rigor os casos ambíguos para auditoria de patologistas humanos.

papers.title: Avaliação de Técnicas de Regularização em um Modelo de Aprendizagem Profunda Aplicado à Classificação de Imagens Gastrointestinais
papers.abstract: Este artigo apresenta uma avaliação do impacto de duas técnicas de regularização, Dropout e Weight Decay, no desempenho de um modelo de rede neural convolucional híbrido aplicado à classificação de imagens endoscópicas do trato gastrointestinal. Utiliza-se a base de dados Kvasir, a qual contém oito classes. A arquitetura combina um backbone DenseNet201 pré-treinado com módulos customizados de Inception, blocos residuais e blocos de atenção (Squeeze-and-Excitation e Contexto Global). Os resultados indicam que a combinação das duas técnicas de regularização melhora a acurácia geral do modelo, embora a confusão entre as classes esophagitis e normal-z-line persista como principal limitação, associada à alta similaridade visual entre essas categorias.

papers.title: Extração de Características e Alinhamento Temporal em Sinais de Áudio: Uma Análise da Técnica MFCC+DTW para Reconhecimento de Padrões Acústicos
papers.abstract: Este artigo apresenta uma análise detalhada da técnica de reconhecimento de padrões acústicos baseada na combinação de Coeficientes Cepstrais de Frequência Mel - MFCC (em inglês, Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients) com Alinhamento Temporal Dinâmico - DTW (em inglês, Dynamic Time Warping). O estudo foi conduzido como parte introdutória de uma pesquisa de mestrado sobre Reconhecimento de Fala aplicado a sistemas de autenticação por palavra-chave, utilizando amostras de voz humana. Foram avaliados o desempenho de classificação, a robustez frente às variações temporais e o custo computacional da abordagem. Os resultados experimentais demonstram que a técnica MFCC+DTW é promissora para identificar padrões acústicos complexos, se comparada à correlação cruzada simples, com custo computacional relativamente baixo. No entanto, observou-se uma sensibilidade que requer ajustes finos nos parâmetros de processamento para otimização da taxa de acerto.

papers.title: Aprendizado Profundo e Regressores de Séries Temporais para Predição Multi-Horizonte da Irradiância Solar no Método Híbrido de Predição
papers.abstract: Resumo: A predição de irradiância solar em curto prazo é essencial para aumentar a confiabilidade operacional de sistemas fotovoltaicos diante da variabilidade atmosférica. Embora o Método Híbrido de Predição (MHP), baseado em imagens hemisféricas all-sky e Machine Learning (ML), tenha demonstrado bom desempenho, ainda não havia sido avaliado sistematicamente com arquiteturas modernas de aprendizado de máquina. Este trabalho apresenta o primeiro benchmark do MHP, comparando modelos de Deep Learning (DL), Time Series Regressors (TSR), a RNA original, um Ensemble e um modelo de Persistência para horizontes de 1, 15 e 30 min, sob protocolo cronológico interanual com validação estatística inferencial. Entre os modelos individuais, a GRU apresentou o melhor desempenho (RMSE = 92,30 W/m²), enquanto o Ensemble obteve o menor erro global (RMSE = 87,42 W/m²), reduzindo o RMSE em 5,3% em relação ao melhor modelo individual e em 16,9% frente à RNA original, além de apresentar a menor variabilidade entre horizontes. Os resultados demonstram que arquiteturas recorrentes superam a RNA originalmente empregada no MHP e que um Ensemble de baixo custo estabelece um novo limite superior de desempenho para predição multi-horizonte.

papers.title: With a Little Help From AI?! Governing Visual Hate Speech Through AI-Assisted Counter-Image Practices
papers.abstract: The attention-grabbing and memorable nature of visuals makes them a powerful vehicle for spreading hate online. As platforms increasingly reconsider or scale back content moderation efforts, user-centered interventions are gaining importance as complementary governance strategies. While prior research demonstrates the effectiveness of empathy-based textual counter speech, little is known about the role of visual counter speech in mitigating hateful imagery. This preregistered study examines the effectiveness of user-centered interventions against visual hate speech. Using an experimental design (N = 666), we tested four interventions against a no-intervention control condition in response to hateful images targeting transgender persons: (a) empathy-based textual counter speech, (b) AI-generated generic counter images, (c) AI-generated specific counter images replicating elements of the original, and (d) platform-issued warning labels. Results show substantial variation across interventions. Empathy-based textual counter speech and AI-generated specific counter images showed the most consistent reductions in amplification-oriented behaviors, particularly forwarding. Visual interventions did not outperform textual counter speech, suggesting that effectiveness depends less on modality and more on the specificity and contextual alignment of the intervention. Furthermore, effectiveness varied with the intensity of the hate content. Interventions were most effective for humor-based, more ambiguously harmful content, whereas their impact diminished for more severe forms of hate. The consistent performance of AI-generated specific counter images further points to the potential of generative AI to provide users with a rapid, low-cost, and accessible means of producing context-sensitive counter speech.

papers.title: Combining PageRank Modularization and Ontology Verbalization for LLM-Based Complex Ontology Matching
papers.abstract: Complex matching remains a challenge in the ontology matching field. Existing approaches are constrained by strong assumptions on their input: instance-based and rule-mining systems require populated ontologies and reliable links between their instances, while systems built on pre-trained encoders operate at the schema level but target primarily simple correspondences. Recent approaches based on Large Language Models (LLMs) are promising, yet they either rely on manually built ontology modules or feed formal serializations directly to the model. This paper proposes a schema-only pipeline that addresses these limitations by integrating (i) an automatic modularization strategy combining the PageRank and Personalized PageRank algorithms, which reduces the search space while controlling the specificity of the extracted context; and (ii) a verbalization module that turns ontology modules into natural language descriptions, exploited both for embedding-based candidate generation and as context in LLM prompts. The approach is evaluated on four datasets of the OAEI Complex track. Relying solely on schema-level information, our matcher achieves competitive performance compared with state-of-the-art complex matching systems.

papers.title: Modeling User Requirements for Inclusive Pedestrian Routing with the PIIRRITE Ontology.
papers.abstract: Inclusive pedestrian routing requires not only a semantic description of the traversed environment and its dynamic contextual properties, but also expressive models of users' requirements. Existing ontology-based user profiling approaches primarily organize user characteristics into taxonomies, providing limited support for representing conditional requirements that can be evaluated against changing environmental properties. Conversely, ontologies describing pedestrian environments focus mainly on spatial and contextual information, with little support for modeling the structure and semantics of user requirements. This paper extends the PIIRRITE ontology with two new modelets for representing user requirements, including the accessibility-related ones, in pedestrian routing. Our model captures user profiles as sets of conditional requirements, distinguishes requirement importance from flexibility, supports recursively composed requirements, and introduces a distance factor mechanism for proximity-sensitive constraints. We validate the ontology by instantiating a knowledge graph of the LyonTech La Doua campus with representative user personas, evaluating SPARQL queries implementing a set of competency questions, and computing an inadequacy score quantifying a route's suitability for a given user profile.

papers.title: STAR-Q: A Web-Based Platform for Annotating Qualified Knowledge Graph Statements in Texts and Tables
papers.abstract: The construction and evaluation of knowledge graph (KG) population systems depend on high-quality, entitygrounded annotated corpora. However, producing such corpora remains a laborious task: general-purpose annotation tools do not often support the grounding of annotations to KG identifiers, rarely handle tabular content, and provide little support for corpus-level quality control. In this paper, we present STAR-Q (Span and Table Annotation for RDF with Qualifiers), an open-source, web-based annotation platform designed to facilitate the annotation of both texts and tables with knowledge graph entities. STAR-Q lets users highlight mentions corresponding to subjects, predicates, objects, and ordered qualifier predicate-value pairs directly in documents, and then disambiguate them to entities and properties defined in a reference knowledge graph through a configurable lookup interface targeting any Wikibase instance. Wikidata is supported out of the box, with its large set of QIDs and PIDs. Private Wikibase deployments, such as enterprise knowledge graphs, can also be registered and selected per corpus. Annotations use a unified component schema covering both textual spans and character ranges within table cells; resolved values may be KG resources, corpus-local entities and relations, or typed literals. Beyond annotation, STAR-Q provides corpus management and import adapters for structured JSON/JSONL, archive-based corpus formats, Label Studio exports, and its own versioned full-corpus JSON. Annotations generated by the tool can be exported in RDF 1.2, either in a "truthy" statement mode or in a "full" mode preserving component-level text and table evidence using well-known ontologies (DCAT, PROV, NIF, CSVW, Web Annotations). Wikidata-grounded statements can additionally be exported as QuickStatements 3.0 commands for direct submission to Wikidata. We demonstrate STAR-Q through two scenarios: a didactic scenario based on Wookieepedia texts annotated with Wikidata entities curated by the WikiProject Star Wars community effort, and an industrial in-use scenario, where technical telecommunications documents are annotated against an enterprise knowledge graph. The tool is open source at https://github.com/ecladatta/star-q.

papers.title: Automatically Building and Updating a Knowledge Graph of MLIP Models
papers.abstract: Complementing the many efforts in providing semantic representations of concepts, notions, and entities in materials science, we report and illustrate a process by which we can automatically build a knowledge graph of the fast evolving field of machine learning applied to the prediction of material properties, focusing on MLIP (Machine Learning Interatomic Potential). This LLM-based process relies on multiple steps, from information extraction in documents and articles to a validation loop using SHACL constraints to detect and correct errors. It is carried out on a model-by-model basis, focusing on the consistency of representation, therefore enabling an iterative construction where the addition of new models is facilitated. We illustrate the process by showing a few interesting aspects that can be queried from a knowledge graph built from the models listed in the Matbench Discovery leaderboard.

papers.title: Towards Ontology-Guided and Traceable GraphRAG for Legal Knowledge in Industrial Maintenance
papers.abstract: Regulatory industrial maintenance relies on legal texts that are numerous, evolving, and highly interconnected. GraphRAG extends Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by integrating knowledge graphs (KGs) into retrieval and answer generation, offering a promising approach for exploiting the semantic relationships embedded in texts. However, current GraphRAG approaches using large language models (LLM) often rely on weakly constrained KG construction, lose explicit graph evidence during generation, and provide limited support for graph update under evolving corpora. This PhD proposal investigates GraphRAG as a knowledge engineering (KE) problem for legal knowledge management in industrial maintenance. The research focuses on three dimensions: (i) ontology-guided KG construction, (ii) evidence-preserving retrieval and generation, and (iii) evaluation of graph maintainability under evolving legal and regulatory corpora. Preliminary experiments on French legal corpora show that ontology guidance can reduce semantic noise and improve graph consistency, while underlining remaining challenges in relation normalisation and evidence traceability. Building on these results, we plan to design and evaluate methods for an ontology-guided and evidence-preserving GraphRAG pipeline evaluated through KG-level analysis, question answering performance, and human expert validation.

papers.title: Knowledge Graphs as External Memory for LLM-based Scientific Assistants
papers.abstract: Scientific assistants must remember the questions, observations, parameters, and intermediate results that accumulate across days or weeks of inquiry, and trace each conclusion back to its evidence. Large Language Models (LLMs) lack such a structured, persistent memory, which causes contextual degradation, hallucinations, and excessive cost from overusing the context window. This thesis proposes a neuro-symbolic architecture that couples an LLM-based agent with a knowledge graph (KG) built on standardized formal languages (RDF, RDFS, OWL 2 RL, SHACL, SPARQL) and reusing existing ontologies (e.g. PROV-O) whenever possible. In contrast to state-of-the-art memory systems, which rely on schemaless or proprietary property graphs, our hypothesis is that grounding agent memory in open standards improves the six memory operations (consolidation, indexing, updating, forgetting, retrieval, compression) through formal reasoning and declarative validation, at a latency overhead that stays negligible relative to the LLM call. We present the problem, three research questions and their hypotheses, a first experimental prototype that implements an end-to-end store-and-retrieve pipeline, and an evaluation plan combining the LongMemEval and LoCoMo benchmarks with a test case in metabolomics.

papers.title: Stochastic approximation with delayed updates: Asynchronous Machine Learning Algorithms study
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the convergence dynamics of stochastic approximation algorithms under delayed gradient updates and their impact on asynchronous machine learning performance. We present a comprehensive case study comparing the asymptotic behavior of stochastic gradient descent with theoretical guarantees from stochastic approximation theory, examining both decaying and constant learning rate regimes. For decaying rates, we verify convergence but demonstrate that high delays necessitate impractical learning rates; for constant rates, we show that systematically exploiting the learning rate and delay relationship enables robust asynchronous learning. Furthermore, we identify that popular adaptive optimizers degrade under delays because of estimating curvature at current rather than delayed iterates. Finally, we propose a theoretically grounded Hessian-based correction framework using modified Newton-Raphson iterations that explicitly account for gradient staleness.

papers.title: A Love Story in Patterns: Twenty years of ontology design patterns, continued with language models
papers.abstract: Twenty years ago, a group of Semantic Web researchers set out to do for ontologies what the Gang of Four did for software. This talk retraces that love story, from NeOn and eXtreme Design to WOP, through an analysis of 788 papers. Language models now generate and match patterns, solving what we could not, while the bottleneck moves to trust. I argue that patterns matter more than ever, as the unit linking models, people and knowledge graphs, and outline the challenges ahead.

papers.title: The Agent Internet A New Evolutionary Phase of the Web and Its Global Impact
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) based software agents are transitioning from one shot assistants to long term actors that plan, negotiate and accomplish tasks with multiple services. This transformation is resulting in what researchers call the Agent Internet, the Agentic Web or the Internet of Agents, in which programs are full-fledged players alongside people. This article summarizes academic surveys, industry studies and public market data from 2025 to 2026 to outline the multi-layered nature of this setup and to consider its pros and cons. According to market estimates, the revenue for agent software is estimated to be around eight billion dollars in 2025 and up to 35-53 billion dollars in 2030. Adoption statistics tell a tale of much experimentation and few pilots taking it to scale. We discuss communication protocols that enable agents to find and trust each other, the as yet undeveloped identity and payment layers and the burden of agent traffic on advertising supported content. But the challenges that we see are not just capabilities, but security, accountability, interoperability, and who pays for content and compute. Finally, we highlight some of the current research and policy gaps and suggest avenues for a responsible construction.

papers.title: ModelMatch: A Lightweight Passive Token-based Fingerprinting of LLMs
papers.abstract: The widespread deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) through black-box APIs raises significant trust and compliance concerns, as users lack guarantees that the responding model matches the one advertised. This opacity enables risks such as silent model substitution for cost reduction or Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks that redirect queries to malicious models. This paper presents MODELMATCH, a passive fingerprinting framework for verifying LLM identity through output-only analysis, without access to internal parameters or logits. The method leverages 69 stylistic and interaction-based features within a hierarchical classification architecture that performs family-level identification, resolution of conflicting identification, and intra-family classification.

papers.title: AgentFlowShield: Defending LLM Agents Against Metadata Side Channels
papers.abstract: Tool-augmented LLM agents produce structured, multi-phase network traffic whose encrypted metadata-packet sizes, inter-arrival times, burst boundaries, and streaming cadence-can reveal which tools were invoked, whether retrieval or memory was used, and coarse properties of the underlying task. We study this leakage in a scoped single-endpoint deployment model and introduce AgentFlowShield, a phase-aware egress shaping layer combining bucket padding, frame aggregation, bounded jitter, tool normalisation, memory envelopes, and a risk-aware controller. On a 6,300-trace controlled testbed we evaluate six inference attacks under no-defence, generic, and phaseaware defences, probe generalisation with a template-disjoint split, and evaluate three defence-aware adversaries. We provide a bounded within-phase size-channel analysis, identify residual leakage channels, and demonstrate the defence architecture in a controlled loopback testbed with synthetic WAN noise. AgentFlowShield-full preserves low engineering overhead (24 % measured latency overhead in the final utility run) but does not eliminate leakage against the strongest standard-split adversaries (97-100% residual AUPRC on A1-A4). Its clearest gains appear in the template-disjoint and policy-aware settings: D9 shows mixed results in unseen-template splits, with workflow-type AUPRC increasing from 0.385 to 0.453 (indicating higher detectability) and tool-type decreasing from 0.512 to 0.490, while policy-aware A1 fusion drops from 0.995 under random padding to 0.442 under D9. The final results therefore show a narrower but more defensible claim: phase-aware shaping helps generalisation-resistant and calibrated attacks, but fixed-envelope defences still leave strong residual standard-split signals.

papers.title: FedWidthKD : Federated Data-Free KD for Width-Heterogeneous DS-CNNs
papers.abstract: Despite the rapid growth of edge computing, deploying collaborative machine learning across heterogeneous devices remains a fundamental challenge in Federated Learning (FL). Existing approaches either assume uniform model architectures across clients or rely on nested subnetworks that may leave parts of the global model insufficiently updated when no full-width client participates. We propose FedWidthKD, a federated learning framework designed to support DS-CNN architectures with heterogeneous client widths. Client models can be narrower than or equal in width to the global model, allowing the server to reconstruct and maintain a full-width model even when no full-width client participates. Our method combines sample-weighted, coverage-normalized aggregation with a warm-up width-expansion procedure that replicates the available channels and applies norm-scaled perturbations to initialize the full-width architecture. We further apply data-free server-side ensemble distillation on procedurally generated inputs to transfer knowledge from the heterogeneous local models to all channels of the global model without using private client data. Experimental results across four image-classification benchmarks show that FedWidthKD is particularly effective under width and statistical heterogeneity. In the heterogeneous-width evaluation, FedWidthKD outperforms the HeteroFL baseline in 22 of 27 comparisons, including 8 of 9 configurations in which no client trains the full-width model.

papers.title: PIIRRITE: An Ontology for Inclusive Itineraries Modeling
papers.abstract: Enabling inclusive pedestrian routing requires capturing users' specific needs and preferences and leveraging environmental characteristics derived from diverse and heterogeneous data sources. In this paper, we introduce PIIRRITE (Pedestrian InclusIve indooR-outdooR ITinerariEs), an ontology designed to serve as a semantic backbone for inclusive pedestrian routing across indoor and outdoor environments. We build on existing domain ontologies such as GeoSPARQL to represent spatial entities and SAREF to attach contextual properties to spatial entities such as accessibility-related characteristics and environmental conditions. Our ontology is developed using the SAMOD methodology through successive modelets driven by a set of competency questions reflecting user requirements. By bringing together heterogeneous spatial and contextual data, the ontology enables querying and reasoning over diverse data sources to support personalized and inclusive itinerary planning. We demonstrate the applicability of our approach through a real-world case study based on the LyonTech La Doua campus.

papers.title: DICF: Domain-Invariant Counterfactual Explanations
papers.abstract: One desired property of counterfactual explanations is plausibility, that is, a resemblance to real-world data. This property can be achieved by constraining counterfactuals lying in the data manifold. Unfortunately, the data often comes from multiple distinct environments (or domains) or changes under distribution shifts. This may alter the counterfactual validity and plausibility. To address this issue, we propose Domain-Invariant Counterfactual Explanations (DICF), a novel self-explaining framework rooted in invariant representation learning. By explicitly disentangling the latent representation into an invariant class space and a domain space, DICF enables counterfactual search within a predictive space, while preserving the domain specificities. We also introduce a dedicated mechanism to learn the distribution of unseen domains. Empirical evaluations on several datasets demonstrate that when the underlying assumption of class and domain independence holds, such as in image data, DICF finds a trade-off between minimizing feature perturbations and maximizing domain preservation. Furthermore, in mixed-type tabular environments, where domain and predictive features are inherently entangled, the framework remains competitive against state-of-theart baselines.

papers.title: Supernetwork Architecture Selection for Deployable Language Models: RAG Assessment of Overhead-Line Insulators on a 2 GB Device for Grid Operator's Maintenance Crews
papers.abstract: Transmission system operators inspecting high-voltage insulator strings using inference using drone capture inference in remote locations need a local LLM assistant that is useful only if its answers are hallucination-free, drawn from operator-held documents and never exceeding what a photograph shows. The assistant presented here is built accordingly, a detector turning photographs into fixed-text findings, retrieval covering 3,780 IEC, CIGRE and IEEE passages and 127 engineer-reviewed question-answer pairs, and code-enforced hallucination guards checking every answer. Because everything runs within the memory restrictions of an edge device such as the 2 GB Arduino UNO Q, the language model must fit the device, so a weight-sharing supernetwork is trained once from Llama 3.2 1B and eleven subnetworks varying in size are extracted and distilled from a Qwen3.5-27B teacher, yielding a deployable model family. Which network is selected is decided by a selection rule, evaluation set and GPT-OSS:20B judge, ranking candidates by answer quality under a hallucination guard gate and memory restrictions. All subnetworks keep guard violations at or below 2.8% and answer the field questions on the device without failure at 2.8 W, the service peaking at 1108 to 1258 MB as quality rises along the memory-quality Pareto frontier from 0.73 to 0.91 and the median 704-token answer lengthens from 79 to 134 s. The shipped network is the fastest of the three tied on quality within 1200 MB, at 0.85, 94 s per answer and 1172 MB.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Marketing
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most influential technologies shaping modern marketing. The rapid growth of digital platforms, customer data, and automated technologies has changed how businesses understand consumers, communicate with audiences, and measure marketing performance. AI enables organizations to analyse large datasets, predict consumer behaviour, personalize communication, automate routine tasks, and generate content. This research paper examines the role of AI in marketing, its major applications, benefits, challenges, ethical concerns, and future implications. The paper argues that AI can significantly improve marketing effectiveness when combined with human creativity, strategic judgment, and responsible data practices. At the same time, concerns regarding privacy, algorithmic bias, misinformation, transparency, and employment demonstrate the need for careful and ethical implementation. The future of marketing is therefore likely to depend on a collaborative relationship between human marketers and intelligent technologies.
